hints: Set up equilibrium equations horizontally and vertically: $T\sin\theta = 32$ and $T\cos\theta = 80$.
Divide the horizontal equation by the vertical equation to obtain $\tan\theta = \frac{32}{80} = 0.4$.
walkthrough: State the equilibrium conditions for the particle under three coplanar forces (horizontal force $P = 32\text{ N}$, downward weight $80\text{ N}$, and tension $T$ along the string at angle $\theta$ to the vertical):

Divide Equation 1 by Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$\frac{T\sin\theta}{T\cos\theta} = \frac{32}{80}$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.4) \approx 21.8014^\circ$$
$$\theta = 21.8^\circ\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

Square and add Equations 1 and 2 to solve for tension $T$:
$$(T\sin\theta)^2 + (T\cos\theta)^2 = 32^2 + 80^2$$
$$T^2(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) = 1024 + 6400$$
$$T^2 = 7424$$
$$T = \sqrt{7424} = 16\sqrt{29} \approx 86.1626\text{ N}$$
$$T = 86.2\text{ N}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

Under static equilibrium with known tension $T = 120\text{ N}$ and weight $80\text{ N}$, resolve vertically:
$$T\cos\theta = 80$$
$$120\cos\theta = 80$$
$$\cos\theta = \frac{80}{120} = \frac{2}{3}$$

Resolve horizontally in equilibrium to find force $P$:
$$P = T\sin\theta$$
$$P = 120\sin(48.1897^\circ) = 120\sqrt{1 - \cos^2\theta} = 120\sqrt{1 - \frac{4}{9}} = 120\sqrt{\frac{5}{9}} = \frac{120\sqrt{5}}{3} = 40\sqrt{5}$$
$$P = \sqrt{8000} \approx 89.4427\text{ N}$$
$$P = 89.4\text{ N}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$
